P.h: Cisco Secure Email Gateway zero-day exploited in the wild again
P.p: Cisco confirmed that a critical zero-day in its Secure Email Gateway, scored 9.8 out of 10, is under active attack. The path traversal flaw lets unauthenticated attackers write files and run root-level commands through crafted email attachments when File Reputation is enabled.
P.s: CISA and Germany's BSI have issued warnings and urgent patching deadlines. Check whether File Reputation is on, apply Cisco's fix now, and review gateways for signs of compromise.

items.h: Plex flaws exploited in the wild to drop a cryptominer
items.d: A honeypot running Plex Media Server 1.43.2 saw live exploitation on October 17. Four chained flaws gave remote code execution, then a cryptominer and a proxy component were downloaded.

items.h: One compromised login exposed California student records
items.d: From May 22 to September 18 an unauthorized party copied student files from an Educational Testing Service SFTP server. Data dates to 2006 and may include names, IDs and test results. No Social Security numbers.

items.h: Symfony ReDoS: one request burns seconds of CPU
items.d: A crafted Cache-Control header triggers regex backtracking before routing or authentication. One request can use up to 12.7 seconds of CPU. Affects Symfony 4.1 on, plus Laravel, Drupal, PrestaShop and Shopware.

items.h: PwnEscape: guest-to-host KVM escape via Linux networking
items.d: An untrusted VM guest can alter IPv4 header bytes after the host kernel validates them. In a lab it enabled host-kernel writes and a host-root helper. The upstream fix validates checksum_start in five IPv4 consumers.

tiles.t: Nikkei: third breach in a month, 1.8M records
tiles.d: Stolen credentials reached a development system on October 7 and exposed 1.83 million cloud-stored records.

tiles.t: Hollys leaks 2.76M pieces of customer data
tiles.d: Temporary files from a past membership overhaul held dates of birth, phones, addresses and emails.

tiles.t: Chinese crime ring hacked Staples for gift cards
tiles.d: 404 Media reports attackers reached an internal Nexus service, dumped heap memory to hijack support sessions and used 4,630 gift cards worth about $425K.

tiles.t: Florida DMV breached via police-stored login
tiles.d: A local police employee stored credentials insecurely, letting attackers steal driver's license data on September 4.

tiles.t: Grok bot spills CEO's bank data in Slack
tiles.d: A read-only finance agent passed balances and expenses to a second bot with Slack access.

P.h: The AI agents nobody meant to build need hard limits
P.p: IT leaders face unsanctioned agents that employees create by accident with approved desktop tools and recurring workflows. Gartner forecasts that 40% of enterprises will demote or shut down agents by 2027 over governance gaps, security risks and unclear ownership.
P.s: The advice: put hard limits on what agents can touch and build education into tool access. A second piece says runtime access controls, audit trails, retrieval and memory must work together as agents roam enterprise systems.

tiles.t: Accenture weighs $1.5B sale of China consulting
tiles.d: JPMorgan is exploring the sale as Beijing restricts foreign advisers at state-owned firms. Accenture is shifting capital to AI.
GPT-6.1 Sol at low reasoning effort reached 86.6%, against 5.4% for GPT-5.6 Sol.

tiles.t: Microsoft exits UK data center deal over power delays
tiles.d: Electricity delays at Nscale's Loughton site could stretch into the 2030s. Nscale says the build continues.

tiles.t: Lenovo AI Express: AI servers in 15 days
tiles.d: Nvidia-backed quick-ship programme with three Blackwell configurations. Orders are capped and checked.

tiles.t: Cloudflare OS adds Asana, Box, GitHub, Notion
tiles.d: New integrations and services partners for enterprise AI workflows.

P.h: Cloudflare cuts its AI review bill by 68%
P.p: Cloudflare lowered its average review cost from $2.43 to $0.77. The biggest single saving came from checking what actually reached the model provider on each session's first request, then ordering messages consistently across commits, merge requests and repositories so the cache hit.
P.s: Its advice: confirm each session's first request really reads from cache, and check that reviewers still find real problems at the effort level you pay for.

items.h: OpenCode hit by account compromise, 1.4% of Console users
items.d: Attackers compromised an older OpenCode system, per TLDR IT. TechCrunch frames it as hackers running up charges on users' AI accounts. Revoke any exposed provider keys.

items.h: Anthropic quietly pitches its own AI safety bill
items.d: Government could block a model only for foreseeable, imminent risk of over $1B damage or serious harm to 50 people. Independent evaluators would report risks within 72 hours.

items.h: US bans DeepSeek AI from civilian government use
items.d: The order covers civilian agencies. Defense Department agencies are excluded.
Adds lazy imports, built-in frozendict and sentinel, a faster JIT and package startup config files.

tiles.d: Also a low-end MacBook Pro, refreshed iMac and iPad mini. Stores sell new products November 6.

tiles.t: Waymo plans to quintuple fleet to 20,000
tiles.d: It raised $5 billion from private credit lenders and runs 4,000 vehicles in 15 US cities.
Quanta calls OpenAI's proof the most significant AI-for-math achievement so far.

tiles.t: Clairic: a new class of extraction model
tiles.d: Extracts and computes values from unstructured input with higher accuracy and lower cost than LLMs, but it can still err.
